So discard your staged changes with discard-changes first, or do the rollback from Operational mode against the Running Datastore. The command must be executed with the commit parameter; the commit-id is optional and if you do not supply one the most recent commit-record is used. It considers all commit records up to the given commit-id, obtains the reverse-commands for each record, and replays them in order from latest to oldest, reverting the datastore to the state it was in prior to that commit-record. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

show commit retrieves commit-record information from the Commit Repository, and it is available only when the commit-tracking policy is enabled, or when a pending Confirmed Commit exists. If neither is true on your node you get nothing back, so enable it with set system-policies commit-tracking enabled; the default for commit-tracking is disabled. Be aware that disabling the policy again clears the commit-repository of all commit-records. Syntax is show commit [<id>|-s=<since>|-n=<number-of-records>], where <id> selects a specific commit-record, -s takes a timestamp and shows all records created since it, and -n selects an exact number of records to return. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Turn on commit history with set system-policies commit-tracking enabled. commit-tracking enables the commit-repository feature: all configuration changes made via the running or candidate datastores are stored as commit-records that can be visualised, compared and rolled back. It takes enabled or disabled and defaults to disabled; disabling it clears the commit-repository of all commit-records. The running datastore writability is the separate writable-running policy, also enabled/disabled with default disabled. Disabling writable-running makes it impossible to issue configure commands via the running datastore, forcing use of the candidate: the CLI only allows add/set/delete in Candidate mode, NETCONF allows edit-config only via the Candidate Datastore, and RESTCONF, gNMI (telemetry still allowed, gNOI still allowed), WebGUI and TL1 all become read-only. Read both back with show system-policies.

The db-passphrase is missing. The system only accepts take-snapshot if the db-passphrase used for DB snapshot encryption is configured, either globally as part of security-policies or locally as a parameter of the command. Set it globally with set security-policies db-passphrase (string 40..200 characters) or pass it inline, for example take-snapshot db-passphrase=***. The passphrase must be a minimum of 40 characters, must not contain any dictionary words, and may use special characters from the 85-character Z85 set. Automatic DB snapshots are not enabled until it is set. Full syntax: take-snapshot [[db-passphrase=]<value>] [[db-instance=]<value>] [[description=]<value>], with db-instance one of temp (default), manual, onehour, oneday, oneweek or rollback, and description a string of 0..128 characters. Access mode is Operational Mode.

Use the template command. A template is a single entry defined by an object/attribute pair plus the value to be used as the default for that attribute. Syntax: add template-<template-group-name>/<template-name> object <value> attribute <value> value <value> [sequence-id <value>] [label <value>] [condition <value>]; set, show and delete use the same AID. object is the object name (e.g. odu), attribute the attribute name (e.g. admin-state), and value is mandatory (e.g. lock). sequence-id is a number in range 1..65535 and defines processing order, lower ids first. label and condition (e.g. service-type=OTU4) are optional. Example: add template-1/FansInMaintenance object card attribute admin-state value maintenance condition card-type=FAN. Access: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

No. A template-group is created with add template-group-<name> [enabled <value>] [label <value>], where enabled takes true or false. The stated default is true only if there is no other template-group enabled, so only one group is enabled at a time. show template-group-<name> [enabled] [label] displays it and delete template-group-<name> removes it. The template-group is a configuration group containing a list of template entries; individual entries are added under it as template-<template-group-name>/<template-name>. label is an optional user label. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add template-group-1.

Use show templates. It is a show-only command that displays the configuration defining the data model for system templates, and it takes no parameters. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: show templates. For the level below it, show template-group-<name> [enabled] [label] displays an individual template group, and show template-<template-group-name>/<template-name> [sequence-id] [object] [attribute] [value] [label] [condition] displays an individual template entry.

No. The unlock command releases a database previously locked with the lock command, but only the session that performed the lock can trigger the unlock. If a session tries to unlock a database that was locked by another session, or a database that is not locked at all, the unlock command fails. There is a built-in escape: a lock is automatically released if the session that performed the lock is closed, so once that operator session terminates the database frees up. After a successful unlock any session can perform configurations and take a new lock. Syntax: unlock [-h], where -h displays help. Access mode: Operational Mode.

Yes, use the validate command. It validates the contents of the specified configuration, covering any CLI command used to edit a configuration datastore by creating, deleting, merging or replacing content. Syntax: validate candidate <candidate> command <string>. The candidate parameter is the candidate datastore that is the target for validation, and command is the command to validate; both are strings with no default. If the command is validated the CLI replies with OK, otherwise the command fails. Multiple CLI commands can be provided in one call if they are separated with a semicolon. Example: validate 'set ne altitude 600'. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

A maximum of 7 rounds of additional-key-exchange can be configured; additional-key-exchange-id takes 1..7 and configuring it is optional. Each round must use a unique key-exchange algorithm, and the rounds must be configured in the same order on both IKE peers: if the configuration does not match, an IKE-CONFIG-MISMATCH alarm is raised. Syntax: add additional-key-exchange-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<number>/<additional-key-exchange-id> dh-group <value>. dh-group values are dhe-2048, dhe-3072, dhe-4096, dhe-6144, dhe-8192, ecp-256, ecp-384, ecp-521, curve-25519, curve-448, ml-kem-512, ml-kem-768, ml-kem-1024. Port level (CHILD-SA) key exchange is derived from IKE. Configuring it brings the IKE session down immediately to renegotiate. For PQC safety configure PPK or at least one of ml-kem-512, ml-kem-768 or ml-kem-1024; ml-kem-1024 is recommended as the strongest.

Use show data-path-encryption. It is a show-only command that displays the datapath encryption attributes and takes no parameters. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: show data-path-encryption. Related global policy is set with the ikev2 command: set ikev2 data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match <match|ignore>, which controls whether the NE validates the certificate subject alternate name against the IKE ID.

Use the encryption-algorithm command, where the algorithm and key length are part of the AID rather than settable attributes: add encryption-algorithm-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<number>/<algorithm>/<key-length>, or without the SPD entry name for the IKE SA form: add encryption-algorithm-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<number>/<algorithm>/<key-length>. show and delete use the same AIDs; there is no set. algorithm values: null, aes-gcm-8, aes-gcm-12, aes-gcm-16, aes-ctr, aes-cbc, aes-ccm-8, aes-ccm-12, aes-ccm-16, chacha20-poly1305. key-length values: none, key-length-128, key-length-192, key-length-256, with default none. number is the proposal number for the IKE SA, range 1..max. Example: add encryption-algorithm-ipsec/GX2/1/aes-gcm-8/key-length-192.

With ike-sa-proposal, integrity-algorithm and dh-group are mandatory on add and prf is optional: add ike-sa-proposal-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<number> integrity-algorithm <value> dh-group <value> [prf <value>]. On set all three are optional. number is the proposal number for the IKE SA, range 1..max. integrity-algorithm values: none, hmac-sha2-256-128, hmac-sha2-384-192, hmac-sha2-512-256, hmac-sha1-160, hmac-sha1-96. dh-group values: dhe-2048, dhe-3072, dhe-4096, dhe-6144, dhe-8192, ecp-256, ecp-384, ecp-521, curve-25519, curve-448, ml-kem-512. prf values: hmac-sha2-256, hmac-sha2-384, hmac-sha2-512, hmac-sha1. protocol-id is read-only and always IKE. Example: add ike-sa-proposal-ipsec/GX2/1 dh-group dhe-2048 prf hmac-sha2-256 integrity-algorithm hmac-sha2-384-192.

The top-level ikev2 object carries a single attribute, data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match. It is a global, L1 encryption-specific policy indicating whether the NE must validate the certificate subject alternate name to match the IKE ID (OPT-IN) or not (OPT-OUT). Permitted values are match and ignore, with no default given. Syntax: set ikev2 [data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match <value>] and show ikev2 [data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match]. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: set ikev2 data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match match.

Read host-card-encryption-capability on the ikev2-local-instance: it indicates whether the card on which this IKEv2 local instance is running supports encryption, with values yes, no, unknown and default unknown. It is a show-only attribute, as is host-card, the reference to the service card running the instance. The local address is governed by local-address-assignment-method (auto or manual, default auto, show only) and local-address, a settable local IPv4 address for the IKEv2 channel with prefix-length 32, default 0.0.0.0. Other attributes: scope (data-path-encryption, management-ipsec, local-address, local-address-assignment-method), admin-state (lock, maintenance, unlock; default unlock), oper-state (enabled, disabled; default disabled), alarm-report-control (allowed, inhibited; default inhibited), label, AID and started-time. Example: set ikev2-local-instance-1-3 local-address 1.1.180.132.

On ikev2-peer, re-key-frequency is the re-key frequency for the IKE SA with the far-end peer, range 3600..86400 seconds, default 28800. re-auth-frequency is the re-authentication frequency, range 3600..604800 seconds, default 43200. The stated rule is that re-key-frequency and re-auth-frequency values must not be multiples of each other, and they must differ by a few minutes so there is a significant interval between re-authentication and re-keying. Associated failure handling: re-key-fail-policy takes kill traffic or continue traffic, default continue-traffic, and re-key-traffic-kill-offset is 0..86400 seconds, default 0, the wait before killing the encrypted data SAs tied to this IKE SA. re-auth-traffic-kill-offset is likewise 0..86400 seconds, default 0, for killing the Child SAs associated with the IKE SA.

With ipsec-sa-proposal, dh-group is mandatory on add and integrity-algorithm is optional: add ipsec-sa-proposal-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<number> dh-group <value> [integrity-algorithm <value>]. On set both are optional. dh-group values: dhe-2048, dhe-3072, dhe-4096, dhe-6144, dhe-8192, ecp-256, ecp-384, ecp-521, curve-25519, curve-448. integrity-algorithm values: none, hmac-sha2-256-128, hmac-sha2-384-192, hmac-sha2-512-256, hmac-sha1-160, hmac-sha1-96. Two read-only attributes appear on show: protocol-id, which is ESP, and esn (Extended Sequence Number support), which is esn. number is the proposal number, range 1..max. Example: add ipsec-sa-proposal-ipsec/GX2/dns/1 dh-group dhe-3072 integrity-algorithm hmac-sha2-512-256.

Yes. ipsec-sa-re-key sets the re-keying trigger for the IPsec child SA with the far-end peer on three axes: add|set ipsec-sa-re-key-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name> [frequency <value>] [bytes <value>] [packets <value>]. frequency is time-based, range 3600..86400 seconds, default 14400. bytes re-keys on the amount of bytes transmitted, range 1048576..max, default 1073741824. packets re-keys on the amount of packets transmitted and takes either disabled or a number in range 1..9223372036854775808, with default disabled. show reports frequency, bytes and packets; delete removes the object. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

The ipsec-spd-entry action attribute indicates the IPsec treatment given to the IP datagrams and takes protect, bypass or discard, with default protect. The mode attribute indicates whether the IPsec session operates in transport or tunnel mode, taking tunnel or transport with default tunnel, so yes, tunnel is the default. priority is mandatory on add (a uint8 value giving precedence among SPD entries). Other attributes: ipsec-protocol is ESP, esn is true or false with default true, anti-replay-window applies when action = protect and is a number in range 32..1024 with default 64, dynamic-ts is disabled or enabled with default disabled, alarm-report-control is allowed or inhibited with default allowed, and description is a string of length 0..128. Example: add ipsec-spd-entry-ipsec/GX2/dns priority 1 action protect.

Create an ipsec-traffic-selector under the SPD entry, then attach the address and port ranges to it. Syntax: add ipsec-traffic-selector-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name> [next-layer-protocol <value>]. next-layer-protocol is the inner protocol taken from the IPv4 protocol field or the IPv6 next header field, and takes any (value 0), opaque (value 255) or a number in range 0-255, with default any. The traffic selector name is a string of length 1..64. Addresses and ports are then added as child objects with the same AID prefix: local-subnet and remote-subnet for the prefixes, and local-ports and remote-ports for the port ranges. Example: add ipsec-traffic-selector-ipsec/GX2/Radius/ts1 next-layer-protocol 17.

Because the start and stop ports are part of the object identifier, not attributes of it. The local-ports command only defines add, show and delete forms: add|show|delete local-ports-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<start>/<stop>. There is no set form, so to change a range you delete the existing one and add the new one. start takes all, opaque or a port number; stop is a port-number with default 0, and the value 0 is only accepted if the starting port is set to all or opaque. Examples: add local-ports-ipsec/GX2/tacacs/ts1/all, and for a single port add local-ports-ipsec/GX1/dns/ts1/53/53. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use the local-subnet command, with the prefix carried in the AID: add local-subnet-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<prefix>. show and delete take the same AID; there is no set form, so changing a subnet means deleting and re-adding it. prefix is a list of ranges of IPv4/IPv6 addresses (unicast, and broadcast for IPv4 only). The traffic selector named in the AID must already exist under the SPD entry. Example: add local-subnet-ipsec/GX2/dns/ts1/101.10.10.1/32. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

That depends on link-security-control on the macsec-entity, which controls the link security policy for handling data packets when the MACsec connection is not available. It takes must-secure or should-secure and defaults to must-secure, so by default the link is required to be secured. Set it with add|set macsec-entity-<name> [link-security-control <value>]. Related attributes on the same object: enabled (true, false; default true) switches the MACsec entity on or off, supporting-facility names the supporting facility, replay-protection is enable or disable, replay-protection-window is the number of packets in the window, range 0..4294967295 with default 0, and alarm-report-control is allowed or inhibited, default inhibited. negotiated-cipher-suite and oper-state are visible on show. Example: add macsec-entity-6-3-3 supporting-facility ethernet-6-3-3.

Use macsec-mka: set macsec-mka-<name> [connectivity-association-key <value>] [connectivity-association-key-name <value>] [mka-policy <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [label <value>] [psk-lifetime <value>] [psk-expiration-warning <value>] [psk-lifetime-enable <value>]. connectivity-association-key is the pre-shared Connectivity Association Key and connectivity-association-key-name its name, each a string of length 0..64. Key server role is read from is-key-server, which identifies whether the local end is the key server; it takes true or false with default false. show macsec-mka-<name> also reports AID, mka-policy, psk-configured-timestamp, psk-lifetime and psk-expiration-warning (range 1..173, default 14 days) and psk-lifetime-enable (enabled, disabled). Example: set macsec-mka-6-3-3 connectivity-association-key 1122334411223344556677889900112233445566778899001122334455667788 connectivity-association-key-name aa.

On the mka-policy object, which is the MACsec Key Agreement policy referenced by the macsec entity related to an ethernet facility. Syntax: add|set mka-policy-<name> [key-server-priority <value>] [macsec-cipher-suite <value>] [confidentiality-offset <value>] [sak-rekey-interval <value>]; show and delete use the same name. macsec-cipher-suite selects the cipher suite for Secure Association Key (SAK) derivation. sak-rekey-interval is the SAK rekey interval in seconds, range 0 or 30..65535, default 30s. key-server-priority is the priority the MKA protocol uses to select the key server. confidentiality-offset specifies the number of octets in an Ethernet frame that are sent in unencrypted plain-text. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use the re-auth command, which performs a re-authentication operation of IKEv2 security associations. Syntax: re-auth [ikev2-peer=]<value>, where ikev2-peer is a reference to the IKE peer object (the IKE SA) and is given as a string. Access mode: Operational mode only. Both AID forms work, for example re-auth ikev2-peer=ikev2-NE202 and re-auth ikev2-peer-ipsec/GX2. Scheduled re-authentication is separate and is set by re-auth-frequency on the ikev2-peer object (3600..604800 seconds, default 43200).

The re-key command performs on-demand re-keying against one of three targets: a data path encryption secure entity, an IKEv2 peer, or an IPsec Child security association (a Security Policy Database entry). Syntax: re-key [ipsec-security-association=]<value> | [ikev2-peer=]<value> | [secure-entity=]<value>. ipsec-security-association points to the IPsec SPD entry object (Child SA), ikev2-peer references the IKE peer object (IKE SA), and secure-entity points to the secure entity object (Child SA); all three take a string. Access mode: Operational mode. Examples: re-key secure-entity=NE202-1-4-L1-1 and re-key ikev2-peer-ipsec/GX.

Add a remote-ports object with start set to all: add remote-ports-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<start>/<stop>. start takes all, opaque or a port number. stop is a port-number with default 0; if the stopping port is not set the system assumes 0, and 0 is only accepted when the starting port is all or opaque, which is why the all form can be given with no stop value. show and delete use the same AID; there is no set form. Examples: add remote-ports-ipsec/GX2/protect1/ts1/all for every port, and add remote-ports-ipsec/GX2/protect1/ts1/49/49 for a single port.

Use the remote-subnet command, with the prefix embedded in the AID: add remote-subnet-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<prefix>. show and delete take the same AID and there is no set form, so a change requires deleting and re-adding. prefix is a list of ranges of IPv4/IPv6 addresses (unicast, and broadcast for IPv4 only). The ipsec-traffic-selector named in the AID must exist under the SPD entry first. Example: add remote-subnet-ipsec/GX2/dns/ts1/102.20.20.2/32. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use the Receiving Secure Channel command: show sc-rx-<name>/<index> [sci-rx] [state] [association-number] [key-identifier] [next-packet-number]. The state attribute is the one that answers 'in use': it is the state of the secure channel as returned by the MKA stack, with values in-use (Secure Association(s) under this Secure Channel are in use) and not-in-use (no Secure Association(s) under this Secure Channel are in use). The AID is built from name, a string of length 0..64, plus index, the Receiving Secure Channel Index (uint8). sci-rx is the Receiving Secure Channel Identifier, a hex-string of length 16. sc-rx is show-only and is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

sc-tx is the Transmitting Secure Channel object and it is show-only; there is no add, set or delete form. The syntax is show sc-tx-<name>/<index> [sci-tx] [state] [association-number] [key-identifier] [next-packet-number], available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. name is a string of length 0..64 and index is the Transmitting Secure Channel Index (uint8). sci-tx is the Transmitting Secure Channel Identifier, a hex-string of length 16. state is the state of the secure channel returned by the MKA stack: in-use means Secure Association(s) under this Secure Channel are in use, not-in-use means none are. It also reports association-number, key-identifier and next-packet-number.

A secure-application uses an X509v3 certificate as its digital identity. Assign it with set secure-application-<id> active-certificate-id <value>; id is a string 0..20, active-certificate-id a string 0..128, and multiple certificates may be listed comma-separated, e.g. set secure-application-gRPC active-certificate-id certX,certY. show secure-application-<id> reports type (server or client), active-certificate-id, in-use (leafref to active-certificate-id), status (enabled or disabled) and verify-client-cert. To require a client certificate set verify-client-cert required, meaning the client certificate is required and validated, as TLS Mutual Authentication needs; the default is disabled, where no client certificate is requested. Changes take effect only for new TLS connections. show secure-applications lists all of them.

Only if you tell it to. The secure-entity attribute re-key-fail-policy indicates the NE's action when re-keying the IKE security association is unsuccessful; the values are kill-traffic and continue-traffic, and the default is continue-traffic, so by default traffic is not dropped. If you set kill-traffic, traffic-kill-offset controls how long the system waits before killing all encrypted data security associations tied to that IKE SA; range 0..86400 seconds, default 0. The related re-key-frequency is the re-key frequency for the IKE SA with the far-end IKE peer, range 3600..86400 seconds, default 28800. All three are settable on add or set, e.g. add secure-entity-NE202-1-4-L1-1 supporting-facility optical-carrier-1-4-L1-1 remote-secure-entity '1-4-L1-1' re-key-fail-policy kill-traffic traffic-kill-offset 300.

No. secure-entity-sa-proposal is a show-only object: show secure-entity-sa-proposal-<name>/<number> [encryption-algorithm] [encryption-key-length] [integrity-algorithm] [dh-group], in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Every algorithm attribute has exactly one permitted value, which is also its default: number is 1, encryption-algorithm is aes-gcm-16, encryption-key-length is key-length-256, integrity-algorithm is none, and dh-group is ecp-521. The integrity-algorithm and dh-group values are the ones advertised to the far-end secure entity peer. So the layer 1 wavelength encryption proposal is fixed at AES-GCM-16 with a 256-bit key and ECP-521, and can only be displayed.

Through the security-policy-database object, whose key is the IKE peer and whose payload is the secure entity. The AID is security-policy-database-<ikev2-local-instance>/<ikev2-peer-name>: ikev2-local-instance is the name (ID) of the local IKE protocol daemon instance and ikev2-peer is a reference to the IKE peer object (IKE SA). The associated-secure-entity attribute is the list of all SPD entries associated with that far-end peer for which IKE negotiates security associations (keys). Use add security-policy-database-<ikev2-local-instance>/<ikev2-peer-name> [associated-secure-entity <value>], with matching set, show and delete forms, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. Example on 1830 GX G40: add security-policy-database-ikev2-local-instance-1-6/ikev2-NE202-1-4 associated-secure-entity secure-entity-1-6-L1-1.

Yes, with a CRL Distribution Point: each manually configured CDP supports download and auto-refreshing of a specified CRL. Use add cdp-<name> url <value> [enabled <value>] [refresh-interval <value>], plus set, delete and show cdps. url is the HTTP URL of the CRL, format http://<host>[:<port>]/<path to crl file>, e.g. http://crl.example.org/pki/myCA.crl. enabled (true/false, default false) turns on automatic download and periodic refresh, and enabling immediately triggers a CRL auto-download; when disabled no refresh occurs but existing CRLs are unaffected. refresh-interval is either the enum use-next-update, taking the next refresh time from the CRL's next-update field, or a duration '[xw] [xd] [xh] [xm] [xs]', e.g. 2w or 5d 12h. show cdp-<name> reports next-update-time, last-update-time and last-update-result. Requires System Administrator privilege.

Use cert-gen, in Operational mode: cert-gen [-f] [certificate-name=]<value> [[days=]<value>] [[org-name=]<value>] [[common-name=]<value>] [[subject=]<value>] [SAN=]<value>] [auto-install <true|false>]. certificate-name is a string of length 1..128. Validity is set by days, the number of days the certificate is valid for, and it defaults to 365. org-name is a string 1..64, common-name is the IP or host name identifying the server (1..64), and subject is the full certificate subject name (1..1024); when generating a self-signed certificate you must specify either subject or common-name. auto-install defaults to true and auto-assigns the certificate to any secure-application that has no active certificate. -f forces the command without confirmation. Example: cert-gen -f certificate-name=self-signed-cert1 days=10 org-name=testorg common-name=testcert auto-install=true.

Through cert-to-name, a prioritized set of rules mapping an X.509 client certificate to a specific user identity; each rule either extracts a username from a certificate field or maps it directly. Syntax: add cert-to-name-<id> map-type <value> field <value> mapped-user-name <value> criteria <value> [priority <value>] [issuer <value>] [enabled <value>] [label <value>], plus set, show and delete. map-type is extract or map. field applies only when map-type is extract: common-name, san-any, san-dns-name, san-ip-address, san-rfc822-name, san-upn, san-uri. mapped-user-name is required only when map-type is map, naming the local or remote user identity. criteria defines the conditions that invoke the rule. priority ranges 1 to 255. issuer (value any) filters certificates from a specific issuer. enabled defaults to True. Example: add cert-to-name-rule_name map-type extract field san-dns-name.

Delete with clear [-f] certificate [type=]<value> [id=]<value>, in Operational mode. type is trusted, local or peer, and id is the certificate ID, a string of length 0..128 that must match a currently installed but unused certificate of that type; press <tab> to list the certificate-ids that can be cleared, and -f skips the confirmation prompt. Examples: clear certificate local certX, or clear certificate type=trusted id=certY. type also accepts bulk purge options instead of a single type: purge-all-invalid, purge-all-unused, purge-all-expired, purge-local-unused and purge-peer-unused. To list what is installed, use show certificates, which displays all managed local/trusted/peer X509v3 certificates on the system that were imported by download mechanism in PKCS#12 or PKCS#7 secure bundles. show certificate-revocation shows certificate revocations.

Use the clear form of crl with a clear-target: clear [-f] crl [[clear-target=]<value>] [crl-name=]<value>, in Operational mode. clear-target values are single-crl (default; removes only the CRL named in <crl-name>, which is then mandatory and must match a currently installed CRL), purge-invalid-crls (purge all invalid CRLs), purge-cached-crls (purge all CRLs automatically cached from a configured CDP or certificate CDP extension) and purge-all-crls. To drop only stale entries run clear crl purge-invalid-crls, which leaves valid CRLs in place. Use <tab> on crl-name to list clearable CRLs, -f to force without confirmation. Check first with show crls or show crl-<name>, which report status (valid, expired, future), type (cached or manually), next-update and associated-cdp. Example: clear crl single-crl myCA-1.

csr-gen creates a local-certificate in the 'pending-import' state and outputs a CSR in PKCS#10 PEM format. That CSR is used with an external Certificate Authority to produce a full certificate, which is then downloaded into the system to produce a complete local-certificate. The command runs in Operational mode: csr-gen [certificate-name=]<value> ([[key-algorithm=]<value>] | [[key-from-certificate=]<value>]) [[signature-hash-algorithm=]<value>] [[metadata-template=]<value>] [[subject=]<value>] [[SAN=]<value>]. key-algorithm defaults to eccp256 (also rsa2048, rsa3072, rsa4096, eccp128, eccp384, eccp521). signature-hash-algorithm defaults to sha256 for rsa2048/rsa3072/eccp256, sha384 for eccp384, sha512 for rsa4096/eccp521. metadata-template defaults to generic. Default key-usage is digitalSignature,keyAgreement; default extended-key-usage serverAuth,clientAuth. Minimal call: csr-gen myCertificate subject='/CN=Nokia'.

Use display-cert with the display-type parameter: display-cert [certificate=]<value> [display-type=]<value>, in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration mode. display-type accepts all-certificate-hierarchy, certificate-details and certificate-hierarchy, defaulting to all-certificate-hierarchy, so the hierarchy is what you get if you specify nothing; use certificate-details for the certificate's own fields only. certificate names the certificate or CSR, e.g. display-cert trusted-certificate-ca_root; typing display-cert alone tab-completes entries such as local-certificate-pace_client and trusted-certificate-ca_root. The details output is the full X.509 dump: version, serial number, signature algorithm, issuer, validity Not Before/Not After, subject, public key info and X509v3 extensions. local-certificate and peer-certificate also expose a trust-chain attribute.

Use the est command. Enrollment over Secure Transport automates certificate requests, renewals and management over HTTPS, replacing the manual CSR process; the device has an EST client that talks to a dedicated EST server. Syntax: est [target-command=]<value> [[est-ca=]<value>] [certificate-name=]<value> ([[key-algorithm=]<value>] | [[key-from-certificate=]<value>]) [[signature-hash-algorithm=]<value>] [[metadata-template=]<value>] [[subject=]<value>] [[SAN=]<value>] [[http-user=]<value>] [[http-password=]<value>]. target-command is cacerts, enroll or re-enroll. est-ca defaults to 1. key-algorithm accepts eccp256, eccp384, eccp251, rsa2048, rsa3072, rsa4096. signature-hash-algorithm is sha512, sha384 or sha256, default sha256. metadata-template defaults to generic. Use http-user and http-password when no valid mTLS certificate exists: est enroll certificate-name=myNewCertificateA subject='/CN=NewCertA' http-user=<username> http-password=<password>.

Yes, via est-ca: set est-ca-<name> [explicit-ca-root <value>] [root-fingerprint <value>] [auto-re-enrollment <value>] [label <value>], with a matching show. auto-re-enrollment specifies when re-enrollment is performed for all leaf certificates issued by that EST CA: a number of days before expiration from 1 to 365, or a percentage of the 'not after date' minus 'not before date' interval rounded up, 10% to 90% in 10% increments, or disabled. The default is Disabled. If auto re-enrollment fails, the RE-ENROLL-FAIL alarm is raised for the affected certificate and re-enrollment is retried once per day until successful or the certificate becomes invalid. The CA is pinned by explicit-ca-root, the trusted root certificate for the EST CA, and root-fingerprint, a SHA-256 or SHA-512 hash verifying the Root CA identity for a secure initial connection. Example: set est-ca-1 auto-re-enrollment 40.

The EST server port is server-port and it defaults to 443. Define servers with add est-server-<name>/<server-name> server-address <value> [server-port <value>] [priority <value>] [enabled <value>] [path-segment <value>], with set, delete and show forms in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Yes, you can define more than one: priority defines the server's precedence and takes a value in the range 1 to 10. If priority is omitted it defaults to the current lowest precedence, that is the highest existing number, plus one; if a priority of 10 already exists the value must be configured manually. server-address is the IP address of the EST server, enabled is True or False with default True, and path-segment is an optional label added to the EST base url, a string of length 0..64. Example: add est-server-1/my-est-server server-address 10.23.55.123 server-port 8443.

Use import-certificate, which imports one or more certificates in PEM format into the NE, in Operational mode: import-certificate {-i, <certificate type>} [<certificate-name>] <string in PEM format> [<passphrase>]. The PEM string is supplied inline. certificate-name is the name the certificate will be known by; if omitted, the name is derived from the topmost certificate issuer /CN plus a numeric suffix, e.g. trusted-certificate-Nokia-1, trusted-certificate-Nokia-2. passphrase decodes encrypted input and applies to trusted-certificate, local-certificate and bundles. -i imports any intermediate certificates present in a PEM string bundle, and for single-certificate files imports intermediates specified through the AIA extension; root certificates must be installed individually. -h shows help. Example: import-certificate peer-certificate certificate-name=peer-cert1 <string in PEM format>.

Check the is-key-in-use attribute on the Image Signing Key: show ISK-<name> [CPU] [key-name] [key-serial-number] [issuer-name] [key-length] [key-payload] [is-key-in-use] [is-key-verified] [being-deleted] [KRK-name] [signature-hash-scheme] [signature-algorithm] [signature-payload] [signature-gen-time], or show ISKs for the list. is-key-in-use indicates if the key is in use in this FRU; true/false, default false. is-key-verified indicates if the key is verified in this FRU; true/false, default false. being-deleted is set to true once the system gets an ISK delete command, meaning deletion is in progress. Remove one with clear [-f] isk [key-name=]<value>, key-name being a string 0..64 and -f forcing without confirmation. Access is Operational Mode, Candidate Configuration Mode only for show. Example: show ISK-1-5-0-ISK_E1.

Use the KRK commands, which show the list of Image Root Keys (KRKs) and KRK information: show KRKs for the full list, and show KRK-<name> [CPU] [key-name] [key-serial-number] [issuer-name] [key-length] [key-payload] for one key, for example show KRK-1-5-0-KRK_E1. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. The attributes are name, the unique representation of the object; CPU, the identifier for member CPUs on cards, starting at 0 (uint8); key-name, a string of length 0..64; key-serial-number, a string; issuer-name, the name of the CSA (Code Signing Appliance), a string of length 0..20; key-length in bits (uint16); and key-payload, the key payload in hex format, a string of length 0..1100. KRK is show-only. The related ISK object reports KRK-name, the name of the KRK that signed that Image Signing Key.

show key-replacement-package displays the key replacement package (KRP) attributes, in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode; it is show-only. Full form: show key-replacement-package [KRP-name] [KRP-version] [key-name] [key-serial-number] [issuer-name] [key-length] [key-payload] [KRK-name] [signature-hash-scheme] [signature-algorithm] [signature-payload] [signature-gen-time] [install-status]. install-status indicates whether this KRP has been installed in the system: not-installed, installing, installed, failed. KRP-version is the package version. issuer-name is the name of the CSA (Code Signing Appliance), string 0..20. KRK-name is the name of the KRK (Image root key) that signed this ISK. signature-hash-scheme is SHA2 256, SHA2 384 or SHA2 512; signature-algorithm is ECDSA, RSA or none; signature-payload is a hex string 0..1024.

Yes, with the revocation-mode attribute of local-certificate: set local-certificate-<id> revocation-mode force-revoked. revocation-mode controls how the revocation status of the certificate is determined and takes auto, force-revoked or force-unrevoked, default auto; force-unrevoked is the opposite override. The same set also accepts alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default allowed) and label (string 0..256). id is a string 1..128. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. show local-certificate-<id> reports revocation-mode plus status (valid, revoked, expired, untrusted, future, pending-import) and used-by, the list of secure-applications, ikev2-peers and similar presently using the certificate. peer-certificate has the identical revocation-mode attribute, values and default.

Add one with add ocsp-server-<name> url <value> priority <value> [enabled <value>], in Operational mode or Candidate Configuration mode; priority is mandatory on add. Order is set by priority, a uint8 in the range 1..10, which sorts the OCSP responders in order of precedence: lower numbered OCSP responders are consulted before higher numbered ones, so priority 1 is tried first. url is the HTTP URL of the responder, format http://<host>[:<port>], host being an IPv4/v6 address or DNS name and port optional, otherwise the default HTTP port 80 is used; length 0..1024. enabled controls whether this server is consulted for revocation status; true/false, default false, so a new responder must be enabled explicitly. name is a string 0..64. Reorder later with set ocsp-server-<name> priority <value>. show ocsp-server-<name> reports url, enabled, priority and last-query. Example: add ocsp-server-1 url http://1.2.3.4:8101 priority 3 enabled true.

A peer-certificate is the X509v3 end-entity certificate representing a trusted 'remote peer' certificate for the L1 encryption secure application. white-listed is read-only in show peer-certificate[-id]: if true, the peer-certificate does not have an associated trust-chain and was explicitly white-listed at import time; otherwise it has an associated trust-chain. Values true/false, default false. The only settable attributes are alarm-report-control (inhibited or allowed, default allowed), label (string 0..256) and revocation-mode (auto, force-revoked, force-unrevoked, default auto). show also returns version (v3), serial-number, subject-name, issuer, trust-chain, valid-from, valid-to, status, public-key-length, public-key-type, certificate-bytes, subject-alternative-names, key-usage and extended-key-usage. status values are revoked, expired, pending-import, untrusted, future, valid and unsupported.

The ssh object controls secure shell access; it is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. Use set ssh [enabled <value>] [port <value>] [pre-login-message <value>] [post-login-message <value>] and show ssh, in Operational mode or Candidate Configuration mode. port is the port listening for ssh login that goes directly to shell; range 1..65535, default 8022. enabled enables direct access to shell via ssh; true or false, default false, so it is off by default and must be turned on explicitly. pre-login-message is the welcome message displayed before user login, a string 0..1440 with no default. post-login-message is displayed after login, also 0..1440, and has a default banner warning that the system is restricted to authorized users for business purposes and may be monitored.

Add an ssh-authorized-key for that user; each entry contains a trusted public key for SSHv2 user authentication. Syntax: add ssh-authorized-key-<user-name>/<key-id> public-key <value> [label <value>], with set ... [label <value>], show ssh-authorized-key-<user-name>/<key-id> [public-key-algorithm] [public-key] [label] and delete ssh-authorized-key-<user-name>/<key-id>. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. user-name owns the key and can be a local or remote user, string 0..32; key-id is a unique identifier for the entry, 1..64. public-key is the SSHv2 (OpenSSH Portable) public key component in PEM format, <key type><SPACE>base64 encoded OpenSSH public key<SPACE><comment>, up to 2048 characters. public-key-algorithm is show-only: ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521, ssh-rsa2048, ssh-rsa3072, ssh-rsa4096.

Use show ssh-host-key to display the global SSHv2 host keys used by both server-side and client-side SSHv2 applications. There must be one host key per supported algorithm, so more than one exists. The system auto-generates a host-key in the default DB, and additional host-keys can be added or overwritten via the ssh-keygen RPC. The public-key-algorithm values are ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521, ssh-rsa2048, ssh-rsa3072, ssh-rsa4096 and ssh-ed25519 (ED25519 support starts at R9.0). Each entry shows public-key (PEM-encoded OpenSSH string, 0..2048 characters), label (0..256 characters), fingerprint-algorithm (md5 or sha256) and fingerprint (0..95 characters). Show a single key with, for example, show ssh-host-key-ecdsa-sha2-nistp521. Access mode is Operational or Candidate Configuration mode.

ssh-keygen generates a private/public key pair and the existing keys in the system are replaced with the newly generated pair. Syntax: ssh-keygen [-b=<key-length>] [-l=<key-label>] [-t=<type>], Operational mode only. -t selects rsa, ecdsa or ed25519, default rsa. -b sets the strength: with secure mode disabled (see security-policies/secure-mode) RSA allows 2048, 3072 or 4096 (default 2048) and ECDSA allows 256, 384 or 521 (default 256); with secure mode enabled RSA allows only 4096 and ECDSA allows 384 or 521 (default 384). ED25519 is 256 regardless of secure mode, and is supported from R9.0. -l sets the key label; if omitted the label is the value of ne-id. Retrieve the new public key with show ssh-host-key.

Create an SSHv2 known hosts entry with add ssh-known-host-<id> address <value> public-key-algorithm <value> public-key <value> [label <value>]. The id is a unique name of 0..64 characters. address is the hostname, IPv4 or IPv6 address of the allowed/known peer host, optionally with a %zone-index for link-local addresses. public-key-algorithm must be one of ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521, ssh-rsa2048, ssh-rsa3072, ssh-rsa4096 or ssh-ed25519 (ED25519 from R9.0). public-key is the OpenSSH host public key in PEM form, <key type><SPACE>base64<SPACE><comment>, 0..2048 characters. label is 0..256 characters. Afterwards use set ssh-known-host-<id> label, show ssh-known-host-<id>, or delete ssh-known-host-<id>. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

The trusted-certificate object holds the X509v3 CA certificates (Root and Intermediate) trusted by the system. Use show trusted-certificate[-id] to view version (v3), serial-number, subject-name, issuer, trust-chain (leafref to /ne/system/security/certificates/trusted-certificate/id), valid-from, valid-to, modification-time, status (in-use, unused, revoked, expired, available, pending-import, invalid, untrusted, future, valid, unsupported), public-key-length (rsa2048/3072/4096, ecdsa256/384/521), public-key-type (rsa, ecdsa), signature-key-type (rsa, ecdsa, rsassa-pss), signature-hash-algorithm (sha256, sha384, sha512, sha1), certificate-bytes, key-usage and extended-key-usage. set trusted-certificate-<id> takes revocation-mode (auto, force-revoked, force-unrevoked; default auto), alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited) and label. Removal is done with the clear certificate command.

Issue terminate cable-id, which stops all running CableID verification tests. The command is available in Operational mode only. Because verification runs on a port-pair basis, the test can only be stopped after the current port-pair verification has finished and before the next port-pair starts: the in-progress port-pair runs to completion, then the test exits. The maximum delay to terminate is one port-pair verification time. Confirm the stop with show cable-id cable-id-status: the test is terminated once cable-id-state changes to idle (from running-incl-switching or running-no-switching). show cable-id lists the cable-id entities; the show form is also allowed in Candidate Configuration mode.

The CableID signal can only be sourced or terminated by the CAD10A and RD20TM cards; the OPSM passes the signal transparently. The CableID path starts at the end A port and terminates at the end Z port, where the signal is sourced or terminated, that is at a CAD10A DWDM port or an RD20TM ADE port. In show cable-id-path-<name>, card-type-a and card-type-z therefore take only the values RD20TM or CAD10A; they are derived from the provisioned fiber-connection at the port-A and port-Z attributes, because when a fiber-connection is created the CableID function checks whether it terminates on a CableID-capable sled and records the card type into the CableID path topology. In R8.0.1 the supported sleds are CAD10A and RD20TM. Use show -r cable-id-path-<name> to also list the supporting fiber connections.

Yes. show cable-id-status [cable-id-state] [test-progress] is the container holding the process status and progress of a CableID-based fiber connection verification, and you may issue show cable-id cable-id-status at any time to query progress. cable-id-state is idle (verification not running), running-incl-switching (running for both active and protected paths) or running-no-switching (running only for the active path); default idle. test-progress is a string (0..255 characters, default None) reading either Not applicable when cable-id-state is disabled, or N out of M completed while running, where M is the total number of port-pairs to be tested and N the number of port-pairs whose testing is complete. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Each carrier can discover up to one node. It is possible for multiple collocated carriers to discover the same node multiple times, each time connected to a different remote carrier. View this with show carrier-neighbor-<local-carrier>, where local-carrier is the local carrier instance that discovered the neighbor node (string 0..16). Displayable attributes are last-update (date-time YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ), age, local-carrier-id (AID of the local carrier), ne-id (0..256), ne-name (0..256), ne-type (0..64), remote-carrier-id (AID of the remote carrier connected to the local carrier, implying a specific remote port id, 0..64), and ipv4-loopback-address and ipv6-loopback-address, which may be empty if not configured. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use show connection-ports-<degree-number>/<index> [port-name]. degree-number must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees, with a range of 1..20. index is a uint32 in the range 1..2 but is always 1 in the 1830 GX, since dwdm-line ports are bi-directional. port-name is an instance-identifier giving the dwdm-line port of the RD or ILAx card; as a consequence the OMS of the corresponding dwdm-port is created. show connection-ports* lists every connection port in the node, for example connection-ports-1/1 with port-name port-1-3-dwdm-line1, and show connection-ports-5/1 shows the single entry for that degree. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use show custom-tlv-<lldp-port>/<direction>/<oui>/<subtype> [value], which lists the Organizational Specific TLV (Type-Length-Value) parameter information. lldp-port is the local port associated with the LLDP agent (string 0..64). direction is ingress or egress. oui is the Organization Unique Identifier of the TLV, the hexadecimal representation of the 24-bit identifier (string 1..6). subtype is the sub-type identifier of the TLV within the scope of the OUI (string 1..507). The command is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

No. The external-fiber-connection is set autonomously by TNMS; although it is possible to configure it manually, it is not recommended to do so. It represents the physical link between two ports of L0 cards in different NEs, or in the same NE in disaggregated configurations. If you do provision one, add external-fiber-connection-<name> requires src-port-name and dst-port-name, with optional label, scope, src-node-id, src-card-name, dst-node-id, dst-card-name and fiber-connection-type (one-way or two-way, default two-way). Before R8.0 you also had to set the port external-connectivity to yes. scope is general-purpose (default) or cable-id; intra-NE connections between RD20TM ADE ports, or between CAD10A DWDM and RD20TM ADE ports, must use cable-id or CableID verification skips them.

fiber-connection is the physical link representation of a connection between two distinct ports (or two distinct sub-ports) in the same NE, used in an OADM/ILA topology. external-fiber-connection is the physical link representation of a connection between two ports of L0 cards in different NEs, or in the same NE in disaggregated configurations. fiber-connection takes label, src-port and dst-port as instance identifiers plus fiber-connection-type (one-way or two-way, default two-way), with the name 0..64 characters. external-fiber-connection instead identifies its endpoints by string names, src-node-id, src-card-name, src-port-name, dst-node-id, dst-card-name, dst-port-name, and adds the scope attribute (general-purpose or cable-id). external-fiber-connection is normally set autonomously by TNMS and manual configuration is not recommended.

Yes. icdp is the Nokia Carrier Discovery Protocol, and its global-switch flag has the value true or false with a default of true, so it is enabled by default. Control it with set icdp global-switch <true|false> and inspect it with show icdp [global-switch] or show topology icdp, which displays icdp global-switch true. The icdp object is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

INCI is the Inter-NE Communication Interface, an API-based communication infrastructure for control plane communication across different network elements, for example between a transponder such as CHM6 on the 1830 GX G40 and a line system such as FLEXILS. It uses gRPC server/client as the core mechanism: when the INCI service is enabled the gRPC server is started and bound to the local IP address, and when an INCI neighbor instance is configured gRPC client sessions are established. The switch is inci-enabled with values true or false and a default of false, so it is not running by default. Enable it with set inci inci-enabled true and check it with show inci [inci-enabled] or show topology inci. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Compare configured-node-name with discovered-node-name on the INCI neighbor. configured-node-name is the user-provisioned name of the remote NE (string 0..128), supplied as a mandatory attribute on add inci-neighbor-<neighbor-id> neighbor-address <value> configured-node-name <value>, and it exists specifically to be compared against the discovered-node-name, which is the name of the remote NE as sent by that remote NE. show inci-neighbor-<neighbor-id> also returns discovered-node-id, the node ID received from the remote node (string 0..12), plus neighbor-address, neighbor-port, connection-status, alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default inhibited) and oper-state (enabled or disabled). Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Two attributes on interface-neighbor control this. discovery-cycle-time is the periodicity at which sndp discover messages are sent, in the range 30..300 seconds with a default of 30. discovery-timeout is the time after which discovery is considered failed, in the range 300..1800 seconds with a default of 300; when this timeout occurs the neighbor-adjacency-state transitions to blackout. Set them with set interface-neighbor-<local-interface> [discovery-cycle-time <value>] [discovery-timeout <value>] [discovery-enabled <value>], where discovery-enabled is true or false with a default of true. neighbor-adjacency-state reports blackout, discovery, holding or unknown (default unknown). The show form also returns neighbor-ne-id, neighbor-ne-name, neighbor-interface-name, neighbor-router-id, neighbor IPv4/IPv6 addresses, last-change-time and oper-state.

No. show links displays the links container within the topology, and these links are dynamically filled in by the system, allowing the NCT topology to be derived and displayed. The command takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. It can also be reached as show topology links, alongside the other topology sub-objects inci, lldp, icdp and sndp. The related nct-connection object, which shows the links between NCT ports in a multi-chassis NE, is likewise dynamically filled in by the system.

The global lldp hold-on-timer sets the time to keep neighbor information in the case where the neighbor does not provide an explicit Time-To-Live (TTL) TLV. It is a number of seconds with a default of 900. Set it with set lldp [hold-on-timer <value>], for example set lldp hold-on-timer 60, and view it with show lldp or show topology lldp. The lldp object is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted; access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. On an individual lldp-neighbor, the ttl attribute gives the number of seconds until the remote system information expires, and if the remote system does not provide a ttl value that parameter is set to the global hold-on-timer.

show lldp-local-info-<lldp-port> displays the LLDP local system information the node sends on that port. chassis-id-subtype is chassis-component and chassis-id (0..255) carries the chassis serial number of the 1830 GX NE. port-id-subtype is local and port-id (0..255) carries the port AID. port-description (0..255) carries the port name and system-name (0..255) carries the NE name. system-description (0..255) is the string Nokia Corporation.Converged OS, Version <release id> build <software label>. supported-capabilities and enabled-capabilities take the values router and bridge. Run show lldp-local-info for all LLDP ports, or for example show lldp-local-info-comm-eth-1-11-ETH4 for the AUX port on a 1830 GX G30. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

No, the egress direction is not supported. show lldp-neighbor-<lldp-port>/<direction> accepts only ingress as the direction in which the neighbor was detected, for example show -r lldp-neighbor-ethernet-1-1-3/ingress or show -r lldp-neighbor-comm-eth-1-11-ETH4/ingress on a 1830 GX G30. The same restriction applies to lldp-port-statistics, whose direction is also ingress only. The lldp-neighbor entry shows the LLDP remote system discovered by the lldp-port and reports last-update, age, chassis-id-subtype and chassis-id, port-id-subtype and port-id, port-description, system-name, system-description, supported-capabilities, enabled-capabilities and ttl. The information is kept indefinitely until the port is decommissioned or the data is manually cleared with clear topology.

No. All counter values in an lldp-port-statistics entry are maintained on a continuing basis and are not deleted upon expiration of the TTL timing counters associated with the LLDP neighbor information. The counters do freeze: all statistical counters associated with a particular port on the local LLDP agent become frozen whenever lldp-admin-status is disabled for that port. show lldp-port-statistics-<lldp-port>/<direction> (direction is ingress only, egress is not supported) reports last-change-time, last-clear-time (default 0000-01-01T00:00:00Z), total-ageouts, which counts the times a neighbor's information is deleted from the lldp-neighbor list due to TTL expiry, plus total-discarded-frames, error-frames, total-frames-in, total-frames-out, total-discarded-tlvs and total-unrecognized-tlvs, all defaulting to 0.

Use show nct-connection-<src-port>/<dst-port> [src-chassis] [dst-chassis] [src-chassis-state] [dst-chassis-state]. It shows NCT connectivity, the existing links between NCT ports in a multi-chassis NE, and these links are dynamically filled in by the system so the NCT topology can be derived and displayed. src-chassis-state and dst-chassis-state take the values node controller, provisioned and unprovisioned, so the controller shelf is the one reported as node-controller. src-chassis and dst-chassis (0..64) give the chassis AID for a commissioned chassis or the chassis serial number for an unprovisioned one. src-port and dst-port must be NCT ports: the port AID for a commissioned chassis, or the format <chassis-serial-number>-<slot>-NCT-<id> for an unprovisioned chassis. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

The sndp command sets or shows the single attribute sndp-enabled, which is the switch controlling the sndp feature. Its values are true or false and the default is true, so sndp is on by default. Use set sndp [sndp-enabled <value>] to change it and show sndp [sndp-enabled] to read it; sndp is also one of the objects viewable under show topology, alongside inci, links, lldp and icdp. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. The related per-interface control is interface-neighbor discovery-enabled, and discovery-cycle-time on interface-neighbor is the periodicity at which sndp discover messages are sent.

add submarine-link-<name> requires the mandatory attributes src-node-id, src-port-name, dst-node-id, dst-port-name and degree-target-tx-power. src-node-id and dst-node-id are the NE names of the source and destination nodes (0..256); src-port-name and dst-port-name identify the OTS port (dwdm-line) of each degree (0..128). fiber-length defines the fiber length in km of the associated fiber pair ID, a decimal64 in the range 0..25000 km with a default of 0, and it does not include the length of the branch segments. Optional attributes include label, src-card-name, dst-card-name, fiber-connection-type (two-way default, one-way), link-name, fiber-pair-id, segment-list (0..512), bu-segment-index (uint16, default 0, and 0 for end nodes), rx-fiber-type, tx-fiber-type, gsnr, degree-expected-rx-power, commissioning-snr-margin, launch-condition (flat-tx or pfib, default pfib) and allocated-spectrum-list, a list of start/end frequency pairs with a maximum of 32 elements.

show supporting-fiber-connection-<name> [fiber-connection-list] shows the list of fiber connections. name is the name of the entity (string 0..64) and fiber-connection-list is an instance-identifier giving the supported fiber connection path. The same container appears under cable-id-path: supporting-fiber-connection is the container holding the fiber-connection-list, and it is displayed when the -r flag is used, as in show -r cable-id-path-1-6-ade6-1-8-ade6, which returns supporting-fiber-connection-1-6-ade6-1-8-ade6 with fiber-connection-list supporting-fiber-connection-R1. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use 'clear [-f] topology [target=]<value>' in Operational Mode. It manually removes existing topology neighbor information. The target is an instance-identifier and may be: an lldp-neighbor instance (discovered via LLDP), a carrier-neighbor instance (discovered via ICMP), or an lldp-port-statistics instance (details associated with an LLDP enabled port). The -f flag forces the command without confirmation. Tip: type 'clear topology <tab>' to list the valid topology objects. Example: clear topology lldp-neighbor-ethernet-1-4-T1-1. The companion 'show topology' (Operational or Candidate Configuration mode) displays inci, links, lldp, icdp or sndp.

Run 'verify [-f] [type-select=]<value> [[target-select=]<value>] [allow-switching]' in Operational Mode. Only type-select=fiber-connection is supported. target-select is the port instance-identifier of the CableID capable card; if omitted, all paths are verified. allow-switching is boolean, default false: false verifies active paths only with no system initiated switching, true allows the CableID function to initiate switching on the OPSM so both active and inactive (working and protection) paths are covered. Precondition: equipment-policies cable-id-control must be enabled. The command prompts for confirmation (-f skips it), is non-blocking, raises the CID-verification-in-progress alarm against the NE until all queued requests finish, and returns verify-result. Check progress with show cable-id-status. Example: verify fiber-connection port-1-6-ade3 allow-switching=true.

The bert command runs in Operational Mode. Start: 'bert start test-id=TestX resource=ethernet-1-6-T1 test-signal-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-monitoring-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-direction=ingress test-signal-monitoring-direction=ingress test-duration=10'. Stop: 'bert stop test-id=TestX'; test-id is mandatory for stop. If you omit test-id on start the system generates a unique one. 100GE/400GE use scrambled-idles, ODU4 uses PRBS31 or PRBS31NONINV, CarrierCTP monitoring uses fec-frames. test-signal-direction and test-signal-monitoring-direction are ingress or egress (default none). test-duration is in seconds, minimum 10 secs, maximum up to 1000 hrs, and the default 0 means an indefinite test. Records are read with 'bert get' (by test-id, resource or AID) and removed with 'bert delete'. Multiple simultaneous BERTs can run on a facility.

You cannot create one. The cid-ptp facility is created by the system when a card supporting the CableID function is created, for example RD20TM or CAD10A, and it represents the CableID SFP and its connection to the card via the CID port. Only set and show are offered (Operational and Candidate Configuration mode): 'set cid-ptp-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>]'. managed-by reads system, and only user-created facilities can be user deleted. admin-state is not editable and the only supported value is unlock; CableID operation is not affected by the cid-ptp admin-state. The read-only 'used' attribute is true when CableID functionality is supported (default false). Example: show cid-ptp-1-4-spcid.

The eth-zr facility is the Digital Coherent 400ZR interface, auto-instantiated when the ZR TOM is provisioned; interface-type is 400ZR (Media-interface 400ZR-CFEC-DP-16QAM) and rate is fixed at 400.000 Gbit/s. fec-type is settable with default ofec; permitted values are not-applicable, cfec, ofec, noFEC, G709, i4 (EFEC-I4), i7 (EFEC-I7), sdfec15, sdfec15nd, staircase7 and ufec7. Degrade is handled by two pairs: FEC Detected Degrade (fdd-monitoring, default disabled; fdd-threshold default 0.0195 avg BER, fdd-clear-threshold default 0.01062 avg BER) and FEC Excessive Degrade (fed-monitoring, default disabled; fed-threshold default 0.0206 avg BER, fed-clear-threshold default 0.01125 avg BER). All four thresholds are decimal64(9) in the range 0.000000001..0.1 avg BER. link-degrade-indication shows none, local-degraded, remote-degraded or local-and-remote-degraded.

The ethernet facility attribute max-packet-length sets the maximum transfer unit in octets. On 1830 GX G30 the range is 1280..18000 octets; on 1830 GX G40 the range is 1518..18000 octets. The default in both cases is 1518. Set it with 'set ethernet-<name> max-packet-length <value>' in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. Two restrictions apply: max-packet-length is configurable on card level only and applies to all interfaces on that card, and it is used only for determining the undersized/oversized packet count in 100GbE PMs.

Use 'show facilities'. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. The output is a flat list of every facility instance on the node, for example super-channel-group-1-4-L1, super-channel-1-4-L1-1, optical-carrier-1-4-L1-1, optical-channel-1-4-L1-1, trib-ptp-1-4-T11, comm-channel-1-4-L1-1, otu-1-4-L1-1-OTUCni, ethernet-1-4-T2 and odu-1-4-L1-1-ODUCni. Use the per-facility commands (for example show ethernet-<name>, show odu-<name>) to see the attributes of an individual entry.

The fc facility (set/show, Operational and Candidate Configuration mode) exposes two Fibre Channel specific attributes for the 32GFC client: tts enables or disables Transmitter Training Signal support, values enabled or disabled with default disabled; and laser-toggling-for-tts enables or disables laser toggling when tts is enabled/disabled, values enabled or disabled with default enabled. The read-only fc-type reports the signal type: FC1G, FC2G, FC4G, FC8G, FC16G or FC32G. Other settable attributes are label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), tx-mapping-mode and expected-mapping-mode (default GMP), loopback (none/facility/terminal, default none), loopback-mode, test-signal-type (default none), test-signal-direction (default ingress) and test-signal-monitoring (default false).

The flexo facility reports foic-type, a read-only attribute naming the FOICx.k interface (k parallel lanes carrying a FlexO-x interface, order x in units of 100G, per G.709.3 FlexO-LR and G.709.1 FlexO-SR). Supported values are foic1.2, foic1.4, foic2.4, foic2.8, foic3.6, foic4.8 and foic4.16, with foic4.8 the default. fec-type is also show-only, default ofec (also not-applicable, cfec, noFEC). resource-mode is the settable one: ADM selects add-drop, XC selects add-drop with regen, and the default is ADM. Example: set flexo-1-5-L1-1 resource-mode 'XC'. Also settable are label, admin-state, alarm-report-control, iid and the fdd/fed raise and clear thresholds.

Creation syntax is 'add flexo-group-<name> carriers <value> rate <value> modulation-format <value> group-id <value> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [fec-type <value>]', in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. The four mandatory arguments are carriers (string 1..32, the carriers bound to the facility), rate (the carried signal basic rate class in Gbit/s), modulation-format (not-applicable, DP-QPSK, DP-16QAM, DP-8QAM or BPSK) and group-id, an integer in the range 1..1048575 that indicates the interface group instance the FlexO-x interface belongs to and must be unique in the NE. Optional fec-type defaults to ofec; admin-state defaults to unlock and alarm-report-control to allowed.

high-speed-monitoring is a small set/show container available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode: 'set high-speed-monitoring [enabled <value>] [port <value>]' and 'show high-speed-monitoring [enabled] [port]'. It has exactly two attributes. enabled is the user configurable switch that turns high speed monitoring on or off, values true or false, default false. port is the user configurable port, a uint16 in the range 1..max, default 57500.

The interlaken facility represents the SPN2 Interlaken interface and is managed with set/show in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Its capacity is a read-only attribute fixed at 500 Gbit/s. managed-by is system only, so it is not user created or deleted. The settable attributes are label (string 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited; default allowed) and loopback (none, facility, terminal; default none, where facility tests towards the facility side and terminal towards the terminal side). Show also returns supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state and avail-state. Example: set interlaken-66-1-8 label interlaken_66_1.

On line-ptp, auto-in-service is controlled by two attributes settable on add and set. auto-in-service-enabled is the auto-in-service switch for the facility, values true or false, default false. valid-signal-time is the configurable time that represents detection of a valid signal used by the auto-in-service mechanism, a number in the range 1..7200 minutes with a default of 480. The read-only remaining-valid-signal-time (1..7200 minutes) shows the actual time left before the facility is automatically enabled by the mechanism. Both are available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode, for example 'set line-ptp-1-2-1 auto-in-service-enabled true valid-signal-time 480'.

They are different objects. network-xconnect is display-only: 'show network-xconnect' takes no parameters and lists the services of the multiple user cross connections commissioned in this NE, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. nw-xconnect is the configurable networking cross-connection entity, supporting add, delete, set and show: 'add nw-xconnect-<name> endpoint1 <value> endpoint2 <value> [xcon-type <value>] [rate <value>]', 'set nw-xconnect-<name> [rate <value>]', 'show nw-xconnect-<name> [AID] [oper-state] [avail-state] [endpoint1] [endpoint2] [xcon-type] [rate]' and 'delete nw-xconnect-<name>'. Use nw-xconnect to create or change a user channel cross-connection, network-xconnect to list what is commissioned.

nw-xconnect supports four xcon-type values, and none of them joins a GCC directly to an OSC: L1-ETH-TO-GCC0 (L1-ETH to GCC0 user channel), L1-GCC0-TO-GCC0 (GCC0 to GCC0), L1-ETH-TO-OSC (L1-ETH to OSC) and L1-OSC-TO-OSC (OSC to OSC). The default is L1-GCC0-TO-GCC0. endpoint1 and endpoint2 are mandatory instance-identifiers: for L1-ETH-TO-GCC0 and L1-ETH-TO-OSC endpoint1 is a comm-eth MO of a chassis; for L1-GCC0-TO-GCC0 endpoint1 is a GCC0 comm-channel MO; for L1-OSC-TO-OSC endpoint1 is an OSCX-5 comm-channel MO. rate is the maximum user channel bandwidth, uint8 range 1..20 Mbps, default 13 for L1-ETH-TO-GCC0 and 20 for L1-ETH-TO-OSC and L1-OSC-TO-OSC. Example: add nw-xconnect-test1 xcon-type L1-ETH-TO-OSC endpoint1 comm-eth-1-16-ETH4 endpoint2 comm-channel-1-6-dwdm-line-OSCX5.

No. The high order ODU is automatically created when an SCH is created. When a CHM6 has an OTU configured on it, use 'show odu' to determine whether the ODU exists. What you create are the low order ODUs: ODU4i (100G) or ODUflexi (400G) facilities represent the low order ODUs that XCONs are mapped into, added with 'add odu-<name> odu-type <value> [parent-odu <value>] [time-slots <value>] ...'. The stated pre-condition is that the super-channel must be added before Low Order ODUs can be added. The read-only class attribute reports high-order for the top-most system-created ODUCn/ODUk, low-order (the default) for children, and mapped for a mapped client signal.

Yes. odu-diagnostics instances are keyed by direction: 'add|set|show|delete odu-diagnostics-<name>/<direction>' where direction is ingress or egress, and each direction has its own values. Per direction you can set tx-tti (hex string with 0x prefix, 1..130 characters, or printable ASCII 1..64) and expected-tti (same forms, default empty), or, in ITU style, tx-sapi/tx-dapi/tx-operator and expected-sapi/expected-dapi/expected-operator (SAPI and DAPI 1..15 ASCII or 1..32 hex, operator 1..32 ASCII or 1..66 hex). tti-style selects ITU-T-G709 (TTI split into SAPI, DAPI and OPER bytes) or proprietary (a single 64 byte string), default ITU-T-G709. Received values are read back with rx-tti, rx-tti-hex, rx-sapi, rx-dapi, rx-operator and their hex forms.

Yes, FEC is on by default. On the otu facility, fec-mode is the configured Forward Error Correction mode on the OTUk/OTUCn client, values enabled or disabled, and it defaults to enabled. fec-generation-mode, the configured FEC generation mode towards the far-end receiver, is also enabled or disabled with default enabled. fec-type defaults to ofec; the permitted values are not-applicable, cfec, ofec, G709, noFEC, i4, i7, sdfec15, sdfec15nd, staircase7 and ufec7. All three are usable on add, set and show, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode, for example 'set otu-<name> fec-mode enabled fec-type ofec'.

Set tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting on the otu-diagnostics instance for the direction concerned. It indicates whether the TTI-Mismatch (TIM) alarm is reported or masked and, when reported, the criteria used. Permitted values are disabled (the default), full-64-bytes, SAPI, DAPI, OPER, SAPI_DAPI, SAPI_OPER, DAPI_OPER and SAPI_DAPI_OPER. To alarm only on a mismatched source trace, use SAPI: 'set otu-diagnostics-1-4-L1-1-OTUCni/ingress tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting SAPI'. direction is ingress or egress and each direction has its own values. Related attributes: tti-style (ITU-T-G709 default, or proprietary) and tim-act-enabled, which decides whether a maintenance signal is inserted per TIM, default disabled.

The stm facility reports stm-type, the type of SDH signal (STM-N), and the supported values are STM-16 and STM-64. stm-type is read-only (show). The facility name follows the Synchronous Transport Module N convention, for example N=16, 64, per ITU-T G.691. Settable attributes include label, admin-state (Lock, Unlock, Maintenance; default Unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), tx-mapping-mode and expected-mapping-mode, tti-style (ITU-T-G709 default, or proprietary), tim-monitor (enabled/disabled, default disabled), tx-tti and expected-tti, loopback-mode (none, facility, terminal; default none) and the test-signal attributes. Example: set stm-1-5-T9.2 tx-mapping-mode BMP.

The trib-ptp attribute tributary-disable-action defines what the network element does towards the client equipment connected over the TOM when a line-side failure is observed, either shutting off the laser or inserting a replacement signal. Values are laser-shut-off (the default), none, odu-ais, send-ais-1, send-gais, send-idles, send-lf, send-ms-ais and send-nos (1830 GX G30 only). tributary-disable-holdoff-timer delays the client shutdown or replacement signal at egress, uint16 range 0..10000 milliseconds, default 0 meaning holdoff is disabled; it applies only when the TDA action is Laser-turnoff. Related switches: near-end-tda (enabled/disabled, default disabled), tda-degrade-mode for BERSD-ODU triggering ALS (default disabled) and forward-defect-trigger (true/false, default true). Example: set trib-ptp-1-5-T2 tributary-disable-action laser-shut-off.

Create with 'add xcon-<name> source <value> destination <value> [payload-type <value>] [direction <value>] [label <value>] [circuit-id-suffix <value>]' in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode; source and destination are instance IDs. direction only accepts two-way, which is also the default. Examples: add xcon-11 source odu-1-1-3-ODU4 destination odu-1-1-1-ODU4-1; add xcon-1 source ethernet-1-4-T1 destination odu-1-4-T1-1-ODUni-1. protection-type is a show-only attribute representing the protection the XCON has, with values y-cable, snc-n, snc-i and unprotected, defaulting to unprotected. Other read-back attributes include type (add, drop, add-drop, express), payload-treatment, network-mapping, circuit-id and managed-by (user by default; only user created XCONs can be user deleted). 'set xcon-<name>' can only change label and circuit-id-suffix.

An L2-bridge is identified by bridge-name, a string of length 0..64 used in the instance name L2-bridge-<bridge-name>. Only set and show are supported, in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode: 'set L2-bridge-<bridge-name> [chassis-name <value>] [description <value>]' and 'show L2-bridge-<bridge-name> [chassis-name] [description]'. There are just two configurable attributes: chassis-name, a leafref giving the chassis associated with this L2 bridge, and description, a string of length 0..255 describing the bridge and its intended purpose. Neither has a default.

Use the clear app command: 'clear [-f] app [app-name=]<value>'. It clears third party apps and is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. app-name identifies the third party app to remove. The -f flag forces the command without confirmation, so omit it if you want the confirmation prompt. The guide lists no other parameters for this command.

Use 'appctl [app-name=]<value> [command=]<value> [[target=]<value>] [[parameters=]<value>[,<value>]*]' in Operational mode or Candidate Configuration mode. app-name is a leafref to the configured third-party-app app-name. command takes restart (restarts the third party application), netls (shows the list of subnet networks used by the containers) or exec (executes a third party application operation given in parameters). target is the scope: either the string system or a chassis/card AID, and it defaults to system. parameters is an optional string list with max-elements 50, applicable when command is restart or exec. None of app-name or command has a default.

Yes. Use the call-home command, syntax 'call-home [dial-out-server-name=]<string>'. It executes a manual connection trigger to a configured dial-out-server and forces a connection attempt. If the dial-out-server is currently in the 'connecting' state, call-home forces an immediate attempt and will not wait before retrying. The dial-out-server-name parameter is the pre-configured name of the dial-out server (string, no default). Access mode is Operational Mode. Pre-condition: the dial-out server must already be configured for the command to execute properly. 'call-home -h' displays help. Examples: 'call-home collector-x' and 'call-home callhome1'. This is also the way to connect a dial-out-server whose auto-connect is set to false.
